Section 1 of 17

Where Did They Go?

Few questions feel more personal than this one.

Someone you loved was alive. You could hear their voice, recognize their laugh, and sit beside them. Then death created an empty place.

Where are they now?

Can they see you?

Can they hear you when you speak to them?

Are they trying to send you signs?

Are they already in heaven, or are they suffering somewhere?

People offer many different answers. Some answers come from family traditions, popular movies, religious teachings, dreams, or personal experiences.

The Bible gives a clear answer built around one great promise: death is a sleep, and Jesus is coming to awaken His people.

How Did Human Life Begin?

To understand death, we first need to understand life.

Read Genesis 2:7 ↗.

The Creator formed the first human being from the dust of the ground. He then breathed the breath of life into him, and the man became a living soul.

Notice the order:

Dust of the ground + breath from the Creator = a living soul

The verse does not say that God placed an immortal soul inside a temporary body. It says the man became a living soul.

A soul is the whole living person.

You do not merely have a soul. In the Bible’s description, you are a living soul.

What Happens When a Person Dies?

Death reverses the process of creation.

Read Ecclesiastes 12:7 ↗.

The body returns to the earth, and the spirit returns to the Creator who gave it.

The word translated “spirit” can also mean breath or life force. It does not mean that a conscious, invisible version of the person leaves the body and continues thinking.

Think of electricity flowing into a lamp.

The lamp plus electricity produces light. When the electricity is removed, the light does not travel somewhere else and continue shining. It goes out.

In a similar way:

Body + breath of life = a living person

Body − breath of life = a dead person

The life-giving power returns to the Creator. The person rests without consciousness until the resurrection.

Is the Soul Immortal?

Many people have been taught that every human being has an immortal soul that cannot die.

Read Ezekiel 18:4 ↗ and Ezekiel 18:20 ↗.

The Bible says, “The soul who sins shall die.”

Read Matthew 10:28 ↗.

Jesus said that both body and soul can be destroyed.

Human beings do not naturally possess immortality.

Read 1 Timothy 6:15–16 ↗.

God alone has immortality within Himself.

Immortality is a gift the Creator will give His people at the resurrection.

Read 1 Corinthians 15:51–54 ↗.

Paul says that mortal human beings will put on immortality when Jesus returns.

We do not already have it. We receive it from the Creator.

Are the Dead Conscious?

Read Ecclesiastes 9:5–6 ↗.

The living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. Their love, hatred, and envy have ended, and they no longer participate in what happens on Earth.

Read Ecclesiastes 9:10 ↗.

There is no work, planning, knowledge, or wisdom in the grave.

Read Psalm 146:3–4 ↗.

When a person dies, their breath leaves and their thoughts perish.

Read Psalm 115:17 ↗.

The dead do not praise the Creator.

These passages do not describe people watching their families from another world. They describe unconscious rest.

The dead are not worried, suffering, lonely, or trapped. They are asleep until the Creator calls them back to life.

Why Does the Bible Call Death a Sleep?

Read John 11:11–14 ↗.

When Lazarus died, Jesus said that His friend was asleep and that He was going to awaken him.

The followers of Jesus thought Lazarus was physically sleeping, so Jesus spoke plainly: “Lazarus is dead.”

Jesus called death sleep because:

  • Sleep is temporary.
  • A sleeping person is unaware of passing time.
  • Sleep ends with awakening.
  • Death will end with resurrection.

Lazarus had been dead for four days.

Read John 11:39–44 ↗.

Jesus did not call Lazarus down from heaven. He called him out of the tomb.

Lazarus awoke when Jesus gave him life.

What Will the Next Moment Feel Like?

A person may remain dead for a few days or thousands of years. Because the dead are unconscious, no time passes in their awareness.

Their final moment is death.

Their next conscious moment is resurrection.

For someone who died trusting Jesus, it will seem as though the voice of the Creator called almost immediately.

Read Job 14:12–15 ↗.

Job expected to rest in the grave until the Creator called him. He trusted that God would remember and desire the person He had made.

The Creator does not forget a face, voice, personality, language, relationship, or story.

Human memory can fail. God’s memory cannot lose you.

When Do God’s People Receive Their Reward?

Read John 5:28–29 ↗.

Jesus said that the dead will hear His voice and come out of their graves.

Read 1 Thessalonians 4:13–17 ↗.

Those who died trusting Jesus will rise when He returns. The faithful living will be gathered with them.

Read Revelation 22:12 ↗.

Jesus says He brings His reward when He comes.

The Bible places the reward at the return of Jesus rather than at the moment of death.

The faithful dead are not already living in heaven. They are resting safely until the resurrection.

What About People Who Rejected the Creator?

Read Revelation 20:5–6 ↗.

The saved are raised at the beginning of the thousand years. This is called the first resurrection.

The lost remain dead during the thousand years. They are raised afterward to face the final judgment.

Read Revelation 20:11–15 ↗.

They are not currently suffering in a place of fire. Their final punishment occurs after the judgment, when sin and death are permanently removed.

The Creator does not keep lost people alive forever for the purpose of tormenting them.

Eternal life is given to those who receive Jesus. The final result of rejecting life is death.

Read Romans 6:23 ↗.

Why Does This Teaching Matter?

If the dead are conscious and able to communicate, then any spirit claiming to be a loved one might appear trustworthy.

If the dead are asleep, such a being cannot be the person it claims to be.

This truth protects us from spiritual deception.

Read Isaiah 8:19–20 ↗.

God’s people are told to seek guidance from Him rather than trying to receive messages from the dead.

The Creator knows your grief. He does not shame you for missing someone.

He invites you to bring that grief directly to Him.

Can Our Ancestors See or Guide Us?

Remembering and honoring those who came before us is not the same as praying to them or seeking spiritual guidance from them.

You can honor family members who have died by:

  • Remembering their lives
  • Preserving truthful stories
  • Passing down helpful knowledge
  • Caring for family and community
  • Learning from both their strengths and mistakes
  • Visiting and caring for burial places
  • Continuing what was good in their example

The Bible records the stories of people from earlier generations so others can learn from them.

Read Hebrews 11:1–40 ↗.

However, the dead cannot hear prayers, provide protection, reveal hidden knowledge, or guide the living.

The Creator asks us to seek Him.

Read Psalm 65:2 ↗ and Hebrews 4:14–16 ↗.

You can speak directly to God. Through Jesus, you have access to the Creator without needing help from the dead.

Does This Teaching Disrespect Native Culture?

Native nations and families do not all hold the same beliefs about death or ancestors.

Every belief should be understood carefully before it is discussed. An entire culture should never be dismissed because of one practice.

At the same time, every spiritual teaching must be tested by Scripture.

That includes teachings found in Native communities, European traditions, popular entertainment, and religious institutions.

The belief that humans possess immortal souls did not begin with Native people. Versions of it have appeared in many cultures and religious systems.

The Bible gives one standard for everyone: the dead are unconscious until the resurrection.

Accepting this teaching does not require rejecting your ancestry, language, family, or people. It means allowing the Creator’s Word to guide your understanding of death.

What About Dreams of Someone Who Died?

Grief can influence dreams.

A dream may include a loved one’s face, voice, mannerisms, or memories. Such a dream can feel very real and may bring comfort or sadness.

A dream about someone does not prove that the dead person visited you.

The human mind continues processing love, loss, fear, and memory while we sleep.

The Creator may sometimes use a dream to direct someone’s attention toward Him, but every dream must still be tested by Scripture.

Read Jeremiah 23:25–32 ↗.

A dream should never be given more authority than God’s Word.

Do not build a belief about death on a dream, feeling, or unexplained event.

What About Near-Death Experiences?

Some people report seeing light, hearing voices, viewing their bodies from outside, or meeting someone during a medical crisis.

These experiences differ greatly from one person to another. They are not all consistent with one another or with Scripture.

A person near death is still alive. Their brain and body may be experiencing trauma, medication, reduced oxygen, altered awareness, or other conditions.

We should treat people’s stories with kindness. We should also test every conclusion by the Bible.

An intense experience does not have greater authority than the Creator’s Word.

Read 2 Corinthians 5:7 ↗.

Faith rests on God’s revealed truth rather than on unusual experiences.

Did the Thief on the Cross Go to Paradise That Day?

Read Luke 23:39–43 ↗.

Jesus told the repentant thief, “Assuredly, I say to you today, you will be with Me in Paradise.”

The original Greek manuscripts did not contain modern punctuation. Translators decided where to place the comma.

Some translations place it before “today,” making the sentence sound like Jesus and the thief entered Paradise that day.

But Jesus Himself had not yet gone to the Father by Sunday morning.

Read John 20:17 ↗.

A reading consistent with the rest of Scripture places the emphasis this way:

“I tell you today, you will be with Me in Paradise.”

Jesus was giving the thief a promise on that dark day. Although Jesus appeared defeated, He assured the man that he would have a place in God’s kingdom.

The thief died with that promise. He now rests until the resurrection.

What About the Rich Man and Lazarus?

Read Luke 16:19–31 ↗.

Jesus told a parable about a rich man and a poor man named Lazarus.

A parable uses a familiar story to teach a spiritual lesson. Not every detail is intended as a literal description.

If the story were a literal picture of the afterlife:

  • Saved people would watch lost people suffer.
  • People in heaven and hell could speak to one another.
  • A drop of water could cool someone in fire.
  • Everyone would fit within speaking distance of Abraham.

The lesson is about how we respond to the Creator’s Word and how we treat people in need.

The rich man ignored Lazarus while he had an opportunity to show mercy. After death, his choice could not be changed.

Jesus ended the story by saying that people who reject Moses and the prophets would not believe even if someone rose from the dead.

The parable teaches us to listen to Scripture now. It does not overturn the Bible’s clear teaching that the dead know nothing.

What About Moses and Elijah?

Read Matthew 17:1–3 ↗.

Moses and Elijah appeared with Jesus.

Elijah never experienced death. The Creator took him to heaven alive.

Read 2 Kings 2:11 ↗.

Moses died, but Scripture gives evidence that the Creator raised him in a special resurrection.

Read Deuteronomy 34:5–6 ↗ and Jude 9 ↗.

Moses and Elijah appeared as representatives of the two groups Jesus will gather when He returns:

  • Those who are raised from the dead
  • Those who are transformed without experiencing death

Their appearance does not teach that all dead people are conscious.

Can Spirits Pretend to Be the Dead?

The Bible teaches that evil angels can deceive people.

Read 2 Corinthians 11:14 ↗.

Satan can appear as an angel of light.

A spiritual being may use familiar information, appearance, or mannerisms to claim the identity of someone who died.

The safest response is not to begin a conversation or seek more evidence.

Return to Scripture and pray directly to the Creator.

Read Deuteronomy 18:10–12 ↗.

God warns against mediums, spiritists, and attempts to contact the dead because these practices open the mind to deception.

The next guide will examine the spirit world and how to recognize what truly comes from God.

Does the Creator Disapprove of Grief?

No.

Read John 11:33–36 ↗.

Jesus wept when Lazarus died.

Grief is a natural response to losing someone you love. Faith does not require you to pretend that death does not hurt.

Read 1 Thessalonians 4:13 ↗.

Paul did not tell people to avoid grief. He said they could grieve with hope.

You may experience sadness, anger, confusion, relief, guilt, or numbness. Grief does not follow one simple schedule.

Bring your real emotions to the Creator.

Seek support from safe family members, friends, counselors, or others who can walk beside you.

Hope does not erase grief. It gives grief a future.

What If Someone Died Before Making Everything Right?

The Creator knows the full story of every life.

He knows what a person understood, what opportunities were available, what wounds influenced them, and how they responded to the Holy Spirit.

You do not have to carry the responsibility of deciding someone else’s eternal future.

Read Genesis 18:25 ↗.

The Judge of all the Earth will do what is right.

Place your loved one in the hands of the Creator. His knowledge is complete, and His love is greater than yours.

Use the time you have now to respond to Jesus and repair relationships while you can.

Does Burial or Cremation Affect the Resurrection?

The Creator formed Adam from the dust.

He is fully able to restore a person whether the body was buried, cremated, lost at sea, destroyed in a disaster, or returned to the earth over many years.

Funeral and burial practices may reflect family, community, and cultural traditions. The Bible does not teach that one method limits God’s ability to resurrect someone.

The hope rests in the Creator’s power, not in the condition of the body.

Read Philippians 3:20–21 ↗.

Jesus can recreate and transform the body completely.

Why Is Resurrection Better Than an Immortal Soul?

The hope of Scripture is not escaping the body. It is the restoration of the whole person.

The Creator made human beings as complete physical, mental, relational, and spiritual beings.

Sin brought death to the whole person.

Jesus brings the whole person back to life.

Read Romans 8:11 ↗.

The same Spirit who raised Jesus will give life to His people.

The resurrection protects several important truths:

  • The Creator alone is the source of life.
  • Death is truly an enemy.
  • Human beings depend completely on God.
  • Jesus truly defeated death.
  • Our hope rests in His return.
  • The whole person will be restored.

The answer to death is not an immortal soul.

The answer is Jesus and the resurrection.

How Should This Truth Change the Way You Live?

Value the life you have now

Time is a gift. Use it to love, forgive, create, serve, and know the Creator.

Speak while people can hear you

Tell people you love them. Apologize when needed. Ask questions while someone is still able to answer.

Seek guidance from the Creator

Bring your prayers to God rather than seeking messages from the dead.

Refuse fear

The dead cannot haunt, watch, curse, or control you.

Grieve with hope

Death creates a painful separation, but the separation is temporary for those who belong to Jesus.

Prepare for resurrection

Place your life in the hands of the One who can awaken the dead.

Think About It

Write your answers in your own words.

  1. What were you taught about death while growing up?
  2. According to Genesis 2:7 ↗, what created a living soul?
  3. What happens to a person’s thoughts at death?
  4. Why does the Bible compare death to sleep?
  5. When do God’s people receive immortality?
  6. Can the dead see, hear, or guide the living?
  7. How can you honor someone’s memory without trying to contact that person?
  8. Why should dreams and near-death experiences be tested by Scripture?
  9. What makes resurrection a stronger hope than the belief in an immortal soul?
  10. Is there grief you need to bring honestly to the Creator?
  11. Who would you most want to see when Jesus raises the dead?

Try This During the Coming Week

Set aside fifteen quiet minutes each day.

Read one passage:

  • Day 1: Genesis 2:7 ↗ and Ecclesiastes 12:7 ↗
  • Day 2: Ecclesiastes 9:5–10 ↗
  • Day 3: Psalm 115:17 ↗ and Psalm 146:3–4 ↗
  • Day 4: John 11:1–44 ↗
  • Day 5: 1 Corinthians 15:42–55 ↗
  • Day 6: 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18 ↗
  • Day 7: Revelation 21:1–5 ↗

After each reading, write down:

  • What does this passage teach about life or death?
  • What false idea does it help correct?
  • What promise gives me hope?
  • How can this truth change the way I live today?

If you are grieving someone, write down a meaningful memory. Thank the Creator for that person’s life and place your unanswered questions in His hands.

A Prayer You Can Pray

Creator God, You are the source of every life. Death hurts, and I miss the people I have lost. Thank You for teaching me that the dead are resting and cannot suffer, watch me, or control me. Protect me from every spiritual deception that pretends to speak in their name. Help me seek guidance from You alone. Comfort my heart and give me hope in the resurrection. I trust You to remember every person and make every judgment fairly. Keep me close to Jesus so that when He returns, I can welcome Him and share in the great reunion. Amen.

Remember This

Human beings become living souls when the Creator joins the body with His breath of life.

The Bible does not teach that every person possesses an immortal soul.

The dead are unconscious and unaware of what happens on Earth.

Jesus compared death to sleep because resurrection will awaken the dead.

The faithful receive immortality when Jesus returns.

The lost are not currently suffering in hell.

The dead cannot hear prayers, guide the living, or send messages.

Dreams, near-death experiences, and spiritual appearances must be tested by Scripture.

Remembering and honoring loved ones does not require contacting them.

Burial or cremation cannot limit the Creator’s power to resurrect.

The biblical hope is the restoration of the whole person.

Death does not have the final word. Jesus does.

Are all spirits good? Can supernatural experiences be trusted? The next lesson explains the difference between loyal angels and evil spirits and shows how the Creator protects us from spiritual deception.
